hero.heading:

hero.description: Keep publishing in WordPress. Build selected experiences with reusable React components. This demonstration shows how the pieces fit together.

image.alt: WordPress content feeds reusable page sections inside a shared website layout.

features.heading: A few building blocks. Many possibilities.

items.title: Content in one place
items.description: Headings, links, images, and page sections are supplied by WordPress or the explicit local sample data.

items.title: A familiar experience
items.description: Every React page uses the same header, footer, spacing, colors, and accessible components.

items.title: Grow one page at a time
items.description: Only deliberately assigned URLs use this frontend. Existing WordPress pages keep their own routes.

items.question: Is this the live Trackier website?
items.answer: No. This is sample content in a local starter. It does not change the live site or make claims about the company.

items.question: Where will the page content come from?
items.answer: In WordPress mode, the server requests published structured fields from the accompanying WordPress integration plugin.

items.question: Can the existing website stay online?
items.answer: Yes. Your web server can send only an explicit list of selected paths to this application, leaving other paths with WordPress.
